page: Amazon Web Services r4.8xlarge is a memory-optimized fourth-generation server instance. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, delivering 32 virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system features 244.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.62 GB per core. It operates on the Xen hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture and includes a 45 MB L3 cache. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% tier. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform weakly. However, the instance leverages its 32 vCPUs to achieve average tier performance in multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached read/write operations remains consistently in the average tier.

This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. The high memory density makes it suitable for database operations, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications. PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations both perform in the average tier, confirming its suitability for memory-heavy transactional workloads. It also supports moderate networking requirements with a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.
